verses.pli: Na tena hoti dhammaṭṭho, yenatthaṁ sāhasā naye; Yo ca atthaṁ anatthañca, ubho niccheyya paṇḍito.
verses.en: You don’t become just by passing hasty judgment. An astute person evaluates both what is pertinent and what is irrelevant.

verses.pli: Asāhasena dhammena, samena nayatī pare; Dhammassa gutto medhāvī, “dhammaṭṭho”ti pavuccati.
verses.en: A wise one judges others without haste, justly and impartially; that guardian of the law is said to be just.

verses.pli: Na tena paṇḍito hoti, yāvatā bahu bhāsati; Khemī averī abhayo, “paṇḍito”ti pavuccati.
verses.en: You’re not an astute scholar just because you speak a lot. One who is secure, free of enmity and fear, is said to be astute.

verses.pli: Na tāvatā dhammadharo, yāvatā bahu bhāsati; Yo ca appampi sutvāna, dhammaṁ kāyena passati; Sa ve dhammadharo hoti, yo dhammaṁ nappamajjati.
verses.en: You’re not one who has memorized the teaching just because you recite a lot. Someone who directly sees the teaching after hearing only a little is truly one who has memorized the teaching, for they can never forget it.

verses.pli: Na tena thero so hoti, yenassa palitaṁ siro; Paripakko vayo tassa, “moghajiṇṇo”ti vuccati.
verses.en: You don’t become a senior by getting some grey hairs; for one ripe only in age, is said to have aged in vain.

verses.pli: Yamhi saccañca dhammo ca, ahiṁsā saṁyamo damo; Sa ve vantamalo dhīro, “thero” iti pavuccati.
verses.en: One who is truthful and principled, harmless, restrained, and self-controlled, attentive, purged of stains, is said to be a senior.

verses.pli: Na vākkaraṇamattena, vaṇṇapokkharatāya vā; Sādhurūpo naro hoti, issukī maccharī saṭho.
verses.en: Not by mere enunciation, or a beautiful complexion does a person become holy, if they’re jealous, stingy, and devious.

verses.pli: Yassa cetaṁ samucchinnaṁ, mūlaghaccaṁ samūhataṁ; Sa vantadoso medhāvī, “sādhurūpo”ti vuccati.
verses.en: But if they’ve cut that out, dug it up at the root, eradicated it, that intelligent one, purged of vice, is said to be holy.

verses.pli: Na muṇḍakena samaṇo, abbato alikaṁ bhaṇaṁ; Icchālobhasamāpanno, samaṇo kiṁ bhavissati.
verses.en: A liar and breaker of vows is no ascetic just because they shave their head. How on earth can one be an ascetic who’s full of desire and greed?

verses.pli: Yo ca sameti pāpāni, aṇuṁthūlāni sabbaso; Samitattā hi pāpānaṁ, “samaṇo”ti pavuccati.
verses.en: One who stops all wicked deeds, great and small, because of stopping wicked deeds is said to be an ascetic.

verses.pli: Na tena bhikkhu so hoti, yāvatā bhikkhate pare; Vissaṁ dhammaṁ samādāya, bhikkhu hoti na tāvatā.
verses.en: You don’t become a mendicant just by begging from others. One who has undertaken domestic duties has not yet become a mendicant.

verses.pli: Yodha puññañca pāpañca, bāhetvā brahmacariyavā; Saṅkhāya loke carati, sa ve “bhikkhū”ti vuccati.
verses.en: But one living a spiritual life, who has banished both merit and evil, who wanders having appraised the world, is said to be a mendicant.

verses.pli: Na monena munī hoti, mūḷharūpo aviddasu; Yo ca tulaṁva paggayha, varamādāya paṇḍito.
verses.en: You don’t become a sage by being sagelike, while still confused and ignorant. The astute one who holds the scales, taking only the best,

verses.pli: Pāpāni parivajjeti, sa munī tena so muni; Yo munāti ubho loke, “muni” tena pavuccati.
verses.en: and shunning the bad— that is a sage, <j>and that is how one becomes a sage. One who sagely weighs both in the world, is thereby said to be a sage.

verses.pli: Na tena ariyo hoti, yena pāṇāni hiṁsati; Ahiṁsā sabbapāṇānaṁ, “ariyo”ti pavuccati.
verses.en: You don’t become a noble one by harming living beings. One harmless toward all living beings is said to be a noble one.

verses.pli: Na sīlabbatamattena, bāhusaccena vā pana; Atha vā samādhilābhena, vivittasayanena vā.
verses.en: Not by precepts and observances, nor by much learning, nor by meditative immersion, nor by living in seclusion,

verses.pli: Phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṁ, aputhujjanasevitaṁ; Bhikkhu vissāsamāpādi, appatto āsavakkhayaṁ. Dhammaṭṭhavaggo ekūnavīsatimo.
verses.en: do I experience the bliss of renunciation not frequented by ordinary people. A mendicant cannot rest confident without attaining the end of defilements.
